subject: Mathematics
source: National Curriculum (KS1 Year 1: number and place value; addition and subtraction within 10)

lessons.title: Counting forwards and backwards within 10
objectives: Count forwards from 0 to 10
Count backwards from 10 to 0

keywords.def: counting up: 1, 2, 3
counting down: 3, 2, 1
a row of numbered squares

starter: Say Bismillah. Count 5 objects on the screen.

teach.heading: Counting forwards
teach.note: Use a number track. Point to each number as the class chants. Pause on a number and ask: what comes next?

teach.heading: Counting backwards
teach.note: Backwards is harder than forwards. Use finger-folding and a rocket countdown. Common error: missing out 7 or 3.

teach.heading: Starting from any number
teach.note: Children practise starting from a number given by you. Ask: which direction are we going?

teach.heading: Missing numbers
teach.note: Show number tracks with gaps. Ask children to explain how they know using counting.

practice: Count from 0 to 10, then back to 0.
independent: Fill the gaps: 10, 9, __, 7, __, 5.
Write the numbers from 0 to 10 in order.
lessons.homework: Count backwards from 10 to 0 to a family member, three times.
lessons.send: SEND: use a physical number line to touch. EAL: learn the number names with gestures. Stretch: count in 2s to 10.

lessons.title: Numerals and number words to 10
objectives: Read and write numerals 0 to 10
Read and write number words one to ten

keywords.def: the digit symbol for a number, like 7
a number written in letters, like seven

starter: How many fingers on two hands?

teach.heading: Same number, three ways
teach.note: Show a picture of 7 dates, the numeral and the word. Link all three. The same quantity can be shown in several ways.

teach.heading: Words one to five
teach.note: Show each word with its numeral and a picture. Use phonics to sound out words. Note tricky words like 'one', 'two' and 'four'.

teach.heading: Words six to ten
teach.note: Point out useful letter clues: six starts with s, ten starts with t. Cover and spell the words.

teach.heading: Match them up
teach.note: Show a matching activity. Ask children to read each word before matching.

practice: Read the word and show that many fingers: three, eight, five.
independent: Match each numeral 1 to 10 to its word.
Write the number words for 4, 7 and 10.
Draw 6 dates and write the numeral and word.
lessons.homework: Write the numbers 1 to 10 as words on a card and put it on your wall.
lessons.send: SEND: use numeral and word cards to match with pictures. Stretch: write words for 11 and 12.

lessons.title: One more and one less
objectives: Say one more than a number within 10
Say one less than a number within 10

keywords.def: the number after; add one
the number before; take one away

starter: Bismillah. Write the numeral for eight.

teach.heading: One more
teach.note: Use cubes and a number track. Say it in a full sentence: one more than 5 is 6.

teach.heading: One less
teach.note: Contrast one more and one less using the same starting number. Ask which direction on the track.

teach.heading: Bar model view
teach.note: Show a tower of cubes. Children see that the tower gets taller or shorter by one.

teach.heading: Mixed questions
teach.note: Include edge cases. One less than 1 is 0. Zero is a number. One more than 9 is 10.

independent: Complete: one more than 3 is __, one more than 7 is __.
Complete: one less than 5 is __, one less than 10 is __.
Make a tower of 6 cubes. Make towers one taller and one shorter.
lessons.homework: Ask a grown-up to say a number to 10 and you tell them one more and one less.
lessons.send: SEND: use cubes to build one more. Stretch: one more and one less than numbers to 20.

lessons.title: Comparing groups: more, fewer and equal
objectives: Compare two groups of objects within 10
Use the words more than, fewer than and equal to

keywords.def: a larger amount
a smaller amount
the same amount

starter: Bismillah. What is one more than 7?

teach.heading: Matching groups
bullets: Pair each cup with a plate.
The group with left over has more.
teach.note: Show 5 cups and 4 plates. Pair them. Ask what is left over. This builds the idea of comparing without counting.

teach.heading: Using the words
teach.note: Model each sentence stem and have the children repeat. Use dates in two bowls as the context.

teach.heading: Count and compare
teach.note: Show groups where the bigger group looks smaller (spaced out dots vs close together). Misconception: bigger-looking group means more.

teach.heading: Make them equal
bullets: Add 2 to B to make them equal.
teach.note: Ask: how many more does B need? This leads to the idea of difference.

practice: Which is more: 7 stars or 5 stars?
Which is fewer: 3 cars or 6 cars?
independent: Draw two groups and say which has more.
Write more than, fewer than or equal to: 5 __ 8.
Make two groups that are equal using 6 objects each.
exit: Is 9 more than or fewer than 6?
Make a sentence using equal to.
lessons.homework: Count the cups and plates in your kitchen and say which group has more.
lessons.send: SEND: physically pair items. Stretch: say how many more or fewer.

lessons.title: Comparing numbers with <, > and =
objectives: Compare numbers to 10
Use the symbols <, > and =

keywords.def: bigger than; the open end faces the bigger number
smaller than; the point faces the smaller number
has the same value

teach.heading: The hungry crocodile
bullets: The crocodile eats the bigger number.
teach.note: Use the crocodile story: the mouth always opens towards the bigger number. Draw the symbol large and let children copy the shape with their arms.

teach.heading: Less than
bullets: Read it: three is less than seven.
The point is at the smaller number.
teach.note: Read symbols aloud with children repeating. Show that 3 < 7 and 7 > 3 mean the same thing.

teach.heading: Equals
teach.note: The equals sign means 'is the same as', not 'the answer comes next'. Establish this early.

teach.heading: Choose the symbol
teach.note: Work through each. Ask children to say the sentence aloud in words.

independent: Write two true statements using < with the numbers 3 and 8.
Draw groups to show 4 < 6.
exit: Write a true statement using > and the numbers 2 and 7.
lessons.homework: Make five comparison cards using any numbers to 10, and choose the correct symbol for each.
lessons.send: SEND: use a symbol card with the crocodile picture. Stretch: compare numbers to 20.

lessons.title: Ordering numbers and ordinal words
objectives: Order numbers to 10 from smallest to largest
Use first, second, third and so on

keywords.def: put in a line from smallest to biggest or biggest to smallest
words that tell the position in a line

starter: Say the number words for 3 and 7.

teach.heading: Smallest to biggest
teach.note: Use number cards. Ask: which is the smallest? Then the next smallest. Ordering means each number is bigger than the one before.

teach.heading: Biggest to smallest
teach.note: Contrast ascending and descending order. Use the words 'smallest' and 'biggest' and also 'least' and 'greatest'.

teach.heading: First, second, third
bullets: Who is first in the line?
teach.note: Line up 5 toys. Ask about positions. Note that ordinal numbers tell position, not how many.

teach.heading: Race to the masjid
teach.note: Use a simple story context. Include a mix of first to fifth and last.

practice: Which toy is 4th in the line?
independent: Order smallest to biggest: 9, 3, 6, 1, 7.
Order biggest to smallest: 4, 10, 2, 8.
Draw 5 stars and colour the 3rd star.
exit: Who is first when the order is Zaynab, Hamza, Idris?
lessons.homework: Line up five toys. Name which is first, second, third, fourth and fifth.
lessons.send: SEND: use number cards that can be moved. Stretch: order numbers to 20.

lessons.title: Number line to 10
objectives: Place numbers on a number line from 0 to 10
Find numbers between other numbers

keywords.def: a line with numbers placed in order at equal gaps
in the middle of two things

teach.heading: A number line
teach.note: Draw a number line from 0 to 10. Point to the zero. Ask why the gaps need to be equal.

teach.heading: Find a number
teach.note: Model counting steps along the line. Ask children to show the position of numbers such as 3, 8 and 10.

teach.heading: Between
teach.note: Ask for numbers between two others. Note that 4 and 5 and 6: only 5 is between 4 and 6.

teach.heading: Hop along
teach.note: Preview the use of the number line for adding. Hop one at a time, counting out loud.

practice: Point to 8 on the number line.
Start at 2, hop forward 3. Where do you land?
independent: Draw a number line from 0 to 10 and mark 2, 5 and 9.
Write the missing numbers: 0, 1, __, 3, __, 5.
Which number is halfway between 0 and 10?
exit: Start at 5 and hop back 2. Where are you?
lessons.homework: Draw your own number line to 10 with a ruler and label each number.
lessons.send: SEND: use a large floor number line or physical track. Stretch: number lines from 0 to 20.

lessons.title: Part-whole: parts and wholes
objectives: Understand that a whole is made of parts
Use a part-whole model with numbers to 10

keywords.def: a smaller amount that makes up a whole
the total amount
a picture with one whole and two parts

starter: Bismillah. Which number is halfway between 0 and 10?

teach.heading: Splitting a group
bullets: 6 dates: 4 are on a plate and 2 are in a bowl.
teach.note: Use real or pictured dates. Show how the whole group splits into two parts. Link to sharing and kindness.

teach.heading: The part-whole model
bullets: Big circle on top is the whole.
Two small circles below are the parts.
Parts join to make the whole.
teach.note: Draw the model. Fill in the whole 6, parts 4 and 2. Say: 4 and 2 make 6.

teach.heading: Missing part
teach.note: Children find the missing part using cubes: take 3 away from 7 and count what is left.

teach.heading: Different ways
teach.note: Show many ways to split 5. Ask: how many different ways can you find? Include 0 and 5.

practice: The whole is 8. One part is 5. What is the other part?
The parts are 3 and 4. What is the whole?
independent: Complete the part-whole models: whole 9, part 4, part __.
Whole 10, part 6, part __.
Find three different pairs of parts that make 7.
exit: Whole 8, one part 3. The other part is ...
lessons.homework: Split 8 objects into two groups in as many ways as you can and write down each way.
lessons.send: SEND: use two-colour counters. Stretch: use three parts for a whole.

lessons.title: Addition as combining groups
objectives: Understand addition as putting groups together
Use the symbols + and = in number sentences

keywords.def: put together to find the total
the symbol for adding
how many altogether

teach.heading: Putting together
teach.note: Combine two groups on screen. Count them all to find the total.

teach.heading: The plus sign
bullets: Read it: three plus two equals five.
teach.note: Link the picture to the number sentence. Remind that = means 'is the same as'.

teach.heading: Write the sentence
teach.note: Work with several pictures. Children say the sentence and the answer in a full sentence.

teach.heading: Order does not matter
teach.note: Show that swapping the numbers gives the same total. Do not name the commutative law but notice it. Starting with the bigger number is quicker.

practice: Write a number sentence for 2 stars and 4 stars.
independent: Draw a picture for 4 + 4 and write the sentence.
Write two addition sentences with a total of 6.
exit: Write an addition sentence with a total of 8.
lessons.homework: Collect 10 small objects. Split into two groups and write the addition sentence.
lessons.send: SEND: use cubes to combine and count all. Stretch: three-number addition such as 2 + 3 + 4.

lessons.title: Adding by counting on
objectives: Add by counting on from the larger number
Use a number line to add within 10

keywords.def: start at a number and count up from there
the bigger of the two numbers

starter: Write a sentence with a total of 5.

teach.heading: Do not count all
teach.note: Contrast counting all (1 to 8) with counting on. Counting on is faster. Put 6 in your head and hold up 2 fingers.

teach.heading: Use the number line
teach.note: Draw hops on the line. Each hop is one. Ask children to say the number they land on after each hop.

teach.heading: Start with the larger
teach.note: Show that starting with the larger number saves effort. Misconception: counting the starting number as one hop.

teach.heading: Practise
teach.note: Quick-fire. Children show the answer on mini whiteboards, then explain their method.

practice: Use the number line to solve 4 + 4.
Which number should you start with in 2 + 6?
independent: Draw hops on a number line for 4 + 5.
Write 3 additions that total 9.
lessons.homework: Use a ruler as a number line to solve 5 + 4, 7 + 3 and 2 + 6.
lessons.send: SEND: use fingers or counters beside the number line. Stretch: add to numbers within 20.

lessons.title: Number bonds to 10
objectives: Know pairs of numbers that make 10
Use bonds to 10 to solve problems

keywords.def: two numbers that add to make a given total
a grid of 10 boxes for showing numbers

teach.heading: Ten frame
teach.note: Show a ten frame with 7 counters. Ask how many more to fill it. 7 and 3 make 10.

teach.heading: Bonds to 10
teach.note: Build the full set. Notice patterns: one number goes up as the other goes down. These are very important facts to learn by heart.

teach.heading: Fingers to 10
teach.note: Use fingers to find bonds quickly. Check understanding with random questions.

teach.heading: Missing numbers
teach.note: Use the ten frame or fingers. Note that the equals sign can come first. Ask what number completes the bond.

independent: Write all the number bonds to 10.
Colour a ten frame to show 10 = 6 + 4.
exit: Write two numbers that add to 10.
lessons.homework: Practise number bonds to 10 using your fingers, 5 times, until you know them quickly.
lessons.send: SEND: use a ten frame with counters throughout. Stretch: bonds to 20 using the tens frame twice.

lessons.title: Fact families: addition and subtraction
objectives: See how addition and subtraction link
Write related number sentences for three numbers

keywords.def: related addition and subtraction sentences using the same numbers
take away

starter: Whole is 9, a part is 5. Other part?

teach.heading: Three numbers
teach.note: Show the part-whole model for 3, 4, 7. Then write the addition sentence.

teach.heading: Four sentences
teach.note: Introduce the minus sign. Point to the whole in each sentence: it is the biggest number. In subtraction it comes first.

teach.heading: Build a family
teach.note: Children write all four sentences. Check that the whole is the largest number.

teach.heading: Spot the odd one out
teach.note: Include a wrong sentence to check understanding. Ask why it cannot be true.

practice: Use 4 + 5 = 9 to write a subtraction fact.
independent: Write four sentences for 3, 6, 9.
Write four sentences for 1, 8, 9.
Complete: 10 - 7 = __ because 7 + __ = 10.
exit: Write one addition and one subtraction sentence using 4, 5 and 9.
lessons.homework: Choose three numbers to 10 that work as a fact family and write all four sentences.
lessons.send: SEND: colour-code the whole. Stretch: write fact families with numbers to 20.

lessons.title: Subtraction as taking away
objectives: Understand subtraction as taking away
Write subtraction sentences using the - sign

keywords.def: remove some from a group
the symbol for subtracting
what remains after taking some away

starter: Bismillah. Write the fact family for 2, 3, 5.

teach.heading: Taking away
teach.note: Use real or pictured dates. Cross out items taken away. Count what is left.

teach.heading: The minus sign
bullets: Read it: six take away two equals four.
The first number is what we start with.
teach.note: Link each part of the sentence to the picture. Common error: reading it as 2 - 6.

teach.heading: Cross out and count
teach.note: Children draw and cross out. Check that they start with all of the group, then cross out the right amount.

teach.heading: Take away to zero
teach.note: Take everything away: nothing left. Take nothing away: the same left. Include as a surprise.

practice: There are 9 stars. Take 4 away. How many are left?
independent: Draw a picture for 7 - 5 and write the sentence.
Write a take-away story using the numbers 8 and 3.
lessons.homework: Use 10 objects. Take some away and write the subtraction sentence three times.
lessons.send: SEND: use counters and a 'take away' tray. Stretch: subtract within 20.

lessons.title: Subtracting by counting back
objectives: Subtract by counting back on a number line
Use bonds to 10 to subtract

keywords.def: start at a number and count down
how much bigger or smaller one number is than another

starter: Say the number bonds to 10 for 4 and 7.

teach.heading: Count back
teach.note: Use fingers: count back 3 as you fold 3 fingers. Do not count the starting number as the first step.

teach.heading: Number line hops
teach.note: Draw backward hops. Ask children to say each number as they land.

teach.heading: Use bonds to 10
teach.note: Link subtraction to number bonds. This is a powerful way to remember subtraction from 10.

teach.heading: Which method?
teach.note: Discuss which method suits which question: 9 - 2 count back; 10 - 6 bonds. Encourage flexibility.

independent: Draw hops on a number line for 8 - 5.
Write three subtractions starting from 10.
lessons.homework: Draw a number line from 0 to 10 and show 9 - 4 and 7 - 2 with hops.
lessons.send: SEND: use a physical number line and a counter. Stretch: counting back from numbers to 20.

lessons.title: Missing number problems
objectives: Find missing numbers in addition and subtraction sentences
Use inverse operations to check

keywords.def: a number we have to find, shown by a box or blank
the opposite operation that undoes another

teach.heading: Find the missing number
teach.note: Use cubes or a part-whole model. 4 is a part, 9 is the whole, the missing number is the other part.

teach.heading: Missing at the start
teach.note: Children often struggle when the blank is first. Return to the part-whole model.

teach.heading: Subtraction blanks
teach.note: Use counting back or fact families. Check by adding: 6 + 3 = 9.

teach.heading: Equals on the left
teach.note: Reinforce that equals means 'the same as'. Show a balance scale picture.

independent: Make up two missing number questions for a partner.
lessons.homework: Write five missing number questions, with answers on the back, for someone in your family.
lessons.send: SEND: use a part-whole model with counters for each question. Stretch: missing numbers within 20.

lessons.title: Word problems and review
objectives: Solve one-step addition and subtraction word problems within 10
Choose whether to add or subtract

keywords.def: the total of all the groups
what remains after some are taken away

teach.heading: Read the story
bullets: What do we need to find?
teach.note: Model reading and underlining numbers. Ask children to retell the story in their own words before picking an operation.

teach.heading: Add or subtract?
bullets: Left, take away, gave away: subtract.
teach.note: Teach key words but warn they are not always reliable. Always visualise the story.

teach.heading: Example: dates
bullets: Layla has 4 dates and gets 3 more.
teach.note: Write the number sentence and the answer sentence. Include units (dates) in the answer.

teach.heading: Example: sharing
teach.note: Link to sharing and kindness. Check the answer makes sense by adding back 5 + 4 = 9.

practice: Ali has 6 pens. He is given 2 more. How many now?
There are 10 birds. 3 fly away. How many are left?
Sara has 5 stickers and Noor has 4. How many altogether?
independent: 8 children are in the room. 5 are boys. How many are girls?
Yusuf reads 3 books on Monday and 6 on Tuesday. How many altogether?
Write your own word problem for 7 - 2 and solve it.
exit: There are 9 apples. 4 are eaten. How many are left?
Mum buys 3 red and 5 green apples. How many altogether?
lessons.homework: Make up and solve two word problems about things at home, one adding and one subtracting.
lessons.send: SEND: act out each story with objects. EAL: pre-teach story vocabulary with pictures. Stretch: two-step problems.
